sources.content: # CLAUDE.md for Ostrel. Ostrel records machine learning training runs: metrics, parameters and model checkpoints. The server is written in Go 1.22 and lives in `server/`; the web dashboard is a React app in `web/`. Build the server with `make server` and start it on port 7340 with `make dev`. Run the Go tests with `make test`. The web app uses pnpm; run `pnpm --dir web test` for its tests. Checkpoints over 2 GB go to object storage, configured by `OSTREL_BUCKET`; smaller ones are stored on local disk under `var/checkpoints`.

Working rules. Database migrations live in `server/migrations` and are numbered with four digits, such as `0042_add_tags.sql`. Never edit a migration that has already merged; add a new one. API handlers return JSON errors with a `code` and a `message` field. Metric names are lowercase with dots, for example `train.loss`. Do not log full parameter dictionaries, because some runs store API keys in them. Before opening a pull request, run `make lint`, which runs golangci-lint and eslint. Squash merges only.

claims.text: The Ostrel development server starts on port 7340.
Ostrel stores checkpoints larger than 2 GB on local disk under var/checkpoints.
Ostrel database migrations are numbered with four digits.
Ostrel API error responses include a code field and a message field.
Ostrel metric names use uppercase letters with underscores.
The Ostrel web dashboard is a React app.
